summary.headline: PSP Projects Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR1,113 crore, with EBITDA up 38% to INR69 crore and PAT up 87% to INR30 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly and half-year revenue, with Q2 revenue of INR1,113 crore (+58% YoY) and H1 revenue of INR1,967 crore (+61% YoY). Q2 EBITDA margin was 6.21% versus 7.10% in the comparable quarter, while H1 EBITDA margin was 6.30% versus 6.12% in H1 FY26. Order book stood at INR12,872 crore (+30% YoY) and H1 order inflow was about INR1,305 crore, including INR675 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% (commitment at the lower end) while saying it internally targets growth above 30%, and kept H2 margin commentary toward about 7%.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY vs INR50 crore; margin vs 7.10% in prior comparable quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR62 crore in Q2; INR91 crore in H1

segments.name: Group projects (Adani-linked)
segments.commentary: Management said about 72% of the order book (INR9,229 crore) is group projects, with analysts told Adani is roughly 75% of the book; work is on cost-plus basis with material escalation reimbursed. Adani projects reportedly carry about 5.5-5.7% margin per analyst, which management did not dispute directly.

segments.name: External projects
segments.commentary: External projects make up about 28% of the order book; the current bid pipeline is over INR7,800 crore, split 52% group and 48% external. Key external projects include Shree Ambaji Mata Temple (INR931 crore), SMC high-rise (INR613 crore) and GIFT City Fintech Building (INR251 crore).

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: About 70% of the order book is in Gujarat and about 25% in Maharashtra, with small projects elsewhere.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% YoY (commitment at 30% lower end); management says internal target is above 30% and cited a potential ~INR4,500 crore FY27 revenue as fair but advised 25-30% as the safer commitment.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR5,000 crore plus, per management; an earlier analyst question cited INR5,000-6,000 crore, and H2 inflow implied at INR3,000-4,000 crore from the bid pipeline.

EBITDA margin: H2 may improve by plus or minus 1%, with management saying it could reach about 7.5%; FY28 margin around 7% on Adani cost-plus structures, with potential to 7.5-8% over time (not committed).
Capex: about INR100 crore further expected in H2 FY27; FY28 onward at 3-4% of revenue.
Management said the company is on track for guidance, with focus on execution, cost control, working capital and selective order inflow for H2.

Mobilisation/unbilled: management expects unbilled revenue to normalise, but said it will vary with project type and certification timing; UP-related receivables (about INR40 crore at March) expected by Q3.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR62 crore in Q2 and INR91 crore in H1 FY27; about INR100 crore more expected in H2. Gross block INR851 crore, net block INR451 crore at 30 September.

Precast facility: maximum capacity cited as about INR250 crore revenue per year; management says the plant is operating at full potential. Small capex of INR5-10 crore planned for machines and moulds; sheds for doubling capacity already in place.
New PSP corporate house (Project Ninety) to commence operations on 4 November 2026; the building was completed in 240 days including MEP and interiors.
Project Ninety precast RCC structure (3 basements, ground floor, 18 upper floors) completed in 121 days.
Workforce 23,000-25,000 (seasonal), up from about 11,000 cited by an analyst last quarter; management says overall market supply is sufficient, with 10-15% shortfall on some projects.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of about INR1,305 crore in H1 FY27, including INR675 crore in Q2 across healthcare, airport infrastructure, office buildings, refurbishment and steel accommodation for Adani Group.

Major order-book projects: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR931 crore, SMC high-rise INR613 crore, GIFT City Fintech Building INR251 crore, Science City Human and Biological Science Gallery INR238 crore, GIFT City residential INR187 crore, Dharoi Dam INR171 crore, Sabarmati Riverfront Phase 2 INR155 crore.

Cost pass-through: Adani work is cost-plus, with material differences reimbursed by the group; workforce-related costs adjusted by about 10%; overall cost impact expected around 7%. Non-Adani cement and steel covered through RBI index.
Payment cycle on Adani bills: about 75% cleared within 7-10 days, the rest within the following month.
Management says precast-enabled faster execution could support better pricing for leasing or captive industrial clients, but Adani benefit so far is faster revenue recognition rather than margin.
Mumbai airport (MIAL) work is ongoing, with CSD (city-side development) at Ahmedabad and Mumbai airports cited; Commonwealth tender announced and PSP to bid.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for order inflow for the remaining months, and whether bid pipeline implies INR3,000-4,000 crore wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY27 order inflow of INR4,000-5,000 crore approximately; later said it still expects INR5,000 crore plus for the year, with H1 at about INR1,305 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 EBITDA margin improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 margin may vary by plus or minus 1% and could reach about 7.5%; a 7% FY28 margin was discussed as the Adani cost-structure estimate, with 7.5-8% possible over time.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue run-rate exceed 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current guidance is 30-35% growth with internal target above 30%, but it prefers to commit to 30%; H2 typically stronger than H1.

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and working capital handled on Adani projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Adani is cost-plus with material differences reimbursed; workforce costs adjusted about 10%; about 75% of bills cleared in 7-10 days, so working capital challenge is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin below 7.5-8% guidance from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most projects are in RCC structure stage where overhead absorption is low; margins should improve as the 70% finishing scope with MEP and interiors runs faster over 6-7 months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex guidance and unbilled revenue normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR100 crore more in H2 FY27 and 3-4% of revenue thereafter; unbilled rose because government bills for last month are pending certification and GST invoicing, and management expects normalisation depending on project type.

qa_highlights.question: Surat Diamond Bourse and UP receivables status?
qa_highlights.answer: No commitment yet on SDB (about INR90 crore stays outstanding). UP receivables: INR810 crore received from pool plus about INR20-25 crore out of about INR40 crore; remaining expected by Q3 FY27.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: H1 EBITDA margin 6.30% and Q2 6.21% are below the ~7% full-year target; analysts flagged that the Adani business margin (about 5.5-5.7% per an analyst) may cap blended margins.
Unbilled revenue at INR632 crore and trade receivables at INR809 crore; management noted government bill certification and GST invoicing delays each quarter.

Expected credit loss provision of about INR8 crore in Q2 (INR8.1 crore doubtful advances per analyst), with management saying ECL of INR3-4 crore is normal annually; an analyst estimated adjusted margin near 6.7%.
Order inflow pace: H1 at INR1,305 crore is well below the INR4,000-6,000 crore full-year expectations discussed on the call.
Receivables from Surat Diamond Bourse (about INR90 crore) have no committed payment timeline.
Labour availability and cost inflation (war-related material price increases noted on SMC and RVNL projects), and Adani concentration of about 72-75% of the order book.
Mobilisation advance INR933 crore, high relative to inventory and receivables; need to watch execution of interior and MEP phases on large projects.
summary.management_tone: Confident on revenue and order book, but cautious on guidance: management repeatedly chose to commit only to the lower end (30% growth, INR4,000 crore plus internal target) and to hedge margin upside (7-7.5% rather than a firm number). Answers on Adani economics and receivables were more evasive, with no segment revenue split and no firm SDB payment timeline.
key_quotes: PSP Projects delivered its highest ever quarter and half yearly revenue.
Of the total order book within group projects account for approximately 72% (INR9,229) crores, while external projects contribute the remaining 28%.
Our order book is almost 75% is Adani and 25% is non-Adani.
Historically, even when we were operating on a cost-plus 22% to 25% model, we were able to achieve margins of around 8.5% to 9%.
So maybe by next quarter, we should be through all the money related to UP or certainly be more.
Therefore, I do not see a significant risk of margins falling below 7%.

adds.what: New PSP corporate house (Project Ninety) office building to commence operations 4 Nov 2026; not revenue-generating productive capacity
Precast facility small capex INR5-10 crore for machines and moulds; sheds for doubling capacity already in place; max capacity ~INR250 crore revenue/yr

growth.why: Management cut FY27 revenue growth commitment to 25-30% (from 30-35%), though internal target is above 30%; backed by INR12,872 crore order book (+30% YoY) and H1 order inflow of INR1,305 crore, with FY27 inflow guided at INR5,000 crore plus, but no major new capacity and utilisation stated as full.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 6.21% vs 7.10% a year ago and H1 at 6.30%; management says H2 could reach about 7.5% (+/-1%), but Adani cost-plus work runs about 5.5-5.7% margin and FY28 is guided around 7%, not committed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Precast plant is at full potential with only INR5-10 crore machine and mould capex planned; the Project Ninety corporate office is not productive capacity, and no new plant or line is announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue INR1,967 crore (+61% YoY) and order book INR12,872 crore (+30% YoY) support growth, but management committed only to 25-30% FY27 growth, down from 30-35%, and H1 order inflow of INR1,305 crore is well short of the INR5,000 crore-plus full-year target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is stated as full, but the capex plan is only about INR100 crore in H2 FY27 and 3-4% of revenue from FY28, with no new plant or land approval discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut its revenue growth commitment to 25-30% from 30-35%, and it said the 30% lower end is the floor it will commit to, with an internal target above 30% kept private.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth commitment was already cut to 25-30%, H1 order inflow is INR1,305 crore against a INR5,000 crore-plus target, and Q2 margin fell to 6.21% from 7.10%, so further slippage is plausible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed; the brief covers only projects and order wins.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow of INR5,000 crore plus
rows.why: H1 inflow was INR1,305 crore, so H2 needs about INR3,000-4,000 crore from a bid pipeline of over INR7,800 crore (52% group, 48% external), and management is still holding the target.

rows.label: Unbilled revenue normalisation
rows.why: Net unbilled revenue is INR632 crore against receivables of INR809 crore, and management expects normalisation with UP receivables of about INR40 crore due by Q3, but the timing depends on certification.

rows.label: Adani cost-plus pass-through
rows.why: Material differences are reimbursed and workforce costs are adjusted about 10%, with overall cost impact around 7%, which supports margin stability on about 72-75% of the book.

tone.note: Management was confident on revenue, order book and cost pass-through, but cautious on guidance, cutting its commitment to 25-30% and hedging margin upside at about 7-7.5%. Analysts pushed on Adani's roughly 5.5-5.7% margin, the Q2 margin drop, the unbilled revenue build and the slow H1 order inflow
